Subject: Patient data mapping & de-identification approach (RFP question set)

Hi Karen / Healix procurement,

Thanks for sending over the RFP addendum — we reviewed section 4 (Data Handling) and have a couple of clarifying notes that will help us return a fully completed mapping document. To make the response as useful as possible we've attached a PHI mapping template and a short playbook that describes our de-identification pipeline.

Quick summary/questions from our side:
- Can you confirm the data domains that will be in-scope for the PoC: claims, EHR notes, lab results, device telemetry?
- Do you require de-identification (safe harbor) or pseudonymization with reversible mapping for debug/traceability? If reversible, please list the positions who should have re-identification privileges.
- Expected retention windows for raw vs transformed data (e.g., 30/90/365 days)?

Attached: PHI_Data_Mapping_Template.xlsx (columns: source_table, field_name, PHI_flag, sample_values, retention_req, notes) and Redwood_Deid_Process.pdf (overview of tokenization, suppression, k-anonymity controls, audit logging).

Proposed next step: if useful we can run a short mapping session (30–45 min) with your data engineering lead to pre-fill the template. Are you available Tuesday morning (PDT)?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redwood_Deid_Process.pdf (PDF, 210 KB)]

From: Dr. Karen Miles <kmiles@healixhealth.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Patient data mapping & de-identification approach (RFP question set)

Hi Logan — thanks for the quick follow up and the templates. A few answers that should help: 

- In-scope for the initial evaluation: EHR notes (unstructured), problem lists, medications, labs. We anticipate device telemetry for phase 2.
- We require pseudonymization with reversible mapping for the PoC so our clinical reviewers can re-identify small samples during validation. Re-identification will be restricted to two roles: "Clinical Validation Lead" and "Security Officer" (we can provide names after SOW).
- Retention: raw ingested payloads should be retained for 90 days; de-identified derivatives retained for 5 years.

A couple of follow-ups:
1) For reversible mapping, can you describe your key management approach and where re-identification keys are stored?
2) Auditing: we need immutable re-identification logs that show who requested re-identification, when, and for what ticket/justification.

We can do Tuesday at 9:30am PDT for the mapping session. Please send a calendar invite and any pre-reads.

Best,
Karen
Dr. Karen Miles
Director of Data Governance, Healix Health
[External attachment: Healix_Roles_Roster.csv (CSV, 12 KB)]

Subject: RE: Patient data mapping & de-identification approach (internal)

Logan / Marissa — internal prep notes before the mapping session with Healix: 

- Key management & reversible mapping: Our reversible pipeline uses envelope encryption where the deid token store is encrypted with a per-customer data key (CMK) managed in the customer's KMS for Private/Dedicated customers; for Hosted we offer a Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed CMKs. We should clarify for Healix whether they require their KMS customer-supplied keys in the PoC.
- Re-identification audit: We do maintain immutable audit entries (append-only) for re-ident calls that include user, timestamp, reason, and request_id; exportable via our console and via structured logs to your SIEM. Need to confirm retention period for audit logs vs. data retention.
- Access control: propose role-based access with MFA and step-up approval for re-identification (two-step: request -> approver). We should offer to include a sample re-ident request workflow in the mapping session.

Action items for the call:
1) Bring short slide on key management options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
2) Prepare example audit log sample and retention options.
3) Pre-fill the PHI mapping template for EHR notes (we have synthetic sample) to speed the call.

I'll draft a 20-min internal checklist and a 40-min mapping agenda.

-Rishi
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
